name: Plain English Profile v1 (controlled-language distillation)
derivedFrom: ASD-STE100 Issue 9 (structure reference only; all rule wording originally written)
licenseNote: original-wording: every rule sentence in this file is originally written; no copyrighted specification text or its word lists is reproduced

sentence.note: One instruction per sentence; one topic per paragraph (with a conclusion first); split sentences longer than about 20 words; keep relative clauses to at most one per sentence

voice.agentUnknownNote: Prefer the active voice and name the doer; when the doer is unknown, say so explicitly (for example 'the source does not state who approved this'); use the passive only when the doer is unknown or unimportant

lexicon: One term, one meaning: use the same word for the same concept throughout the text
Prefer everyday words; explain a technical term in plain words where it first appears
Keep noun phrases short (about three words at most); do not stack nouns
Use verbs in simple finite forms; do not reuse one word with several grammatical functions
Make quantities and conditions explicit: give units with numbers and write ranges precisely

avoid.bad: Long noun chains such as 'system configuration item version verification procedure'
avoid.why: Stacked nouns hide who does what to what

avoid.bad: Sentences where several things happen with only 'and' or 'which' to hold them together
avoid.why: Readers lose track of the main statement
The reader cannot act on an unspecified amount or condition

avoid.bad: Idioms and figurative verbs (for example 'the market tanked')
avoid.why: Figurative language does not survive translation and puzzles non-native readers

rewriteExample.before: The implementation of the utilization of this procedure is performed by the operator.
